# Introduction — the tables we own

This folder is ours for the ten days. Three tables, three shapes.

- **Panel A** (`panel-A.csv`) — body measures (`bdims`): height, weight, waist, hip, chest, age, sex. Stand-in for NHANES when that package is not on the machine.
- **Panel B** (`panel-B.csv`) — GSS 2010: `degree`, `grass`, hours of work and rest. `mntlhlth` is *days* of poor mental health — a Quant. Do not mosaic it.
- **Panel C** (`panel-C.csv`) — gapminder 2007: life expectancy, GDP per capita, population by country.

Talk (B) and tape-measure (A) are different hunts.

```{r}
#1 label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(ggformula)
library(skimr)
library(mosaic)
```

We load from this folder:

``` r
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)

A <- read_csv("panel-A.csv")
B <- read_csv("panel-B.csv")
C <- read_csv("panel-C.csv")
```

Found tables train the mark. A campus Free Hunch, if we collect one, is a **made** panel of the same pair type — new people, old grammar. It does not replace A, B, or C.

# Panel A — body / measure

*height_cm, weight_kg, waist_cm are Quant. sex is Qual.*

### 2. Ask

One question *this* table can answer. One it cannot. Write both.

### 3. Choose a mark

Geom, map mark, or (later) test that matches the pair type. Name it before you code.

Who is heavier between men and women ? -Histogram

What is the proportion of men and women ? -Bar

How does waist size vary for men and women ? -Histogram

How does hip size vary for men and women ? -Density

How does chest size vary for men and women ? -Density

which sex has a larger variation in the age range in the given data-set ? -Histogram

Who is taller between men and women ? -Histogram

what are the age ranges in the given data set? -Bar

what is the variation in chest size in the given data set? -Density

what is the variation in waist size in the given data set? -Density

what is the variation in hip size in the given data set? -Density

what is the variation in height in the given data set? -Density

what is the variation in weight in the given data set? -Density

What do we think we will see? One sentence, before Run.

Human brick first. Optional: one AI prompt, pasted below, only for what section 3 named.

``` r
# human chunk

```

Who is heavier between men and women ?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_histogram(~weight_kg,fill =~sex,bins = 50)
```

What is the proportion of men and women ?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_bar(~sex,fill=~sex)
```

How does waist size vary for men and women ?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_histogram(~waist_cm,fill=~sex)
```

How does hip size vary for men and women ?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_density(~hip_cm,fill=~sex)

```

How does chest size vary for men and women ?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_density(~chest_cm,fill=~sex)
```

which sex has a larger variation in the age range in the given data-set ?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_bar(~ age, fill = ~ sex)
```

Who is taller between men and women ?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_histogram(~height_cm,fill =~sex,bins = 50)
```

what are the age ranges in the given data set?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_bar(~ age)
```

what are the age ranges in the given data set?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_density(~ weight_kg)
```

what is the variation in height in the given data set?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_density(~ height_cm)
```

what is the variation in waist size in the given data set?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_density(~ waist_cm)
```

what is the variation in hip size in the given data set?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_density(~ hip_cm)
```

what is the variation in chest size in the given data set?

```{r}
myPanelAData |> gf_density(~ chest_cm)
```

### 6. Say

We all found the density graph comparing chest sizes of men and women interesting because according to the graph, men have a bigger chest size than women which is quite unexpected. Men also have larger variation in the sizes while women have more difference in density for different sizes. This is surprising because according to the bar graph, the ratio of women is slightly more than men, in comparison. We also found the density graph comparing hip size of men and women surprising because it is contrasting the general belief that women have wider hips.

### 7. Limit

What this panel cannot do. Which kit table we refused to abuse.

```{r}
myPanelAData |> group_by(sex) |> summarize (mean_chest_cm = mean(chest_cm,na.rm=T))
```

```{r}
mosaic::t_test(chest_cm ~ sex, data= myPanelAData)

```
